hypothesis: A 128-query, 256-thread attention block raises occupancy from four to eight warps per SM (shared memory still allows one block) and reads each K/V tile once per 128 queries instead of 64, while every query row keeps the same 32-key tile walk and bfloat16 rounding, so outputs stay bit-identical.
independent_variable: Only the flash-attention launch tile: flash_kernel<64,128> versus flash_kernel<128,256>.

fixed_controls.shape: Hq=24, Hk=4, head dim 256, ldv=Hk*head_dim (Qwen3.5-27B full attention)
fixed_controls.inputs: seeded mt19937 20261101, incompressible random bfloat16, same buffers for both arms
fixed_controls.protocol: 1 excluded warmup pair per length, then interleaved A B B A, 10 repetitions, each sample is the mean of 5 launches between two CUDA events, medians per length, two independent trials per device
fixed_controls.cache_stream: warm cache, no clock changes, one non-blocking stream per process
fixed_controls.quality: byte comparison of both arms at every length, prefix windows at q_base 64/128/1024 against the full pass, compute-sanitizer memcheck

run_budget: 10 A-B-B-A repetitions per length per trial, two trials per device; nothing added after seeing results.

acceptance.fidelity: Byte-identical outputs at every measured length; 0 sanitizer errors; attention kernel tests pass with the wide block active.
acceptance.latency: Lower median at every enabled length on each measured device; 512 rows stays on the 64-query block, where the wide tile is 4.9% slower on L20.
acceptance.scope: sm_89 and sm_120 only, windows of at least 640 rows; H200/sm_90, the shared-prefix kernel and end-to-end serving are unverified.

stop: Stop on any parity mismatch or sanitizer error, or at the end of the budget.
